newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says delays daily U.S. lumber exports data.
newsitem.headline: Canada says delays daily U.S. lumber exports data.

text.p: Canada's International Trade Department on Wednesday said it had temporarily suspended the release of daily lumber exports to the United States statistics due to the change in the system for processing export permits.

"Permit processing for quarter three shipments is being held, pending the conversion from a first-come-first-serve to an allocation system targeted for the weekend of October 12, 1996," Claudio Valle, director of the trade controls policy division said in a statement.
"Therefore at this time daily statistics are not being produced. Once quarter 3 processing begins, daily statistics will resume," Valle said.

Under an agreement between Ottawa and Washington, which became effective on April 1, Canadian lumber exports which exceed 14.7 billion board feet annually or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly are subject to export fees.
On Wednesday, Canada officially said it had exceeded its quarterly quota for the second quarter (July 1 - Sept 30), but did not say by how much.
"Accordingly, fees are now being charged for outstanding quarter 2 shipments," Valle said. --Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
